## Bugs in the two files under review

**1. `src/report.js:5-8` — `totalsByMonth` is an unimplemented stub that returns `{}`** (critical)
The `// TODO: group by month` body just returns an empty object, so `report()` maps zero entries and returns `""`. It also leaves both imports (`parseCsv` is used, `toCents` is not) as evidence the intended body never landed.

**2. `src/report.js:13-15` — output order depends on insertion order, not a sorted month key** (minor/latent, no failing test)
`Object.entries(totals)` is unsorted; the tests happen to feed rows in chronological order so sorting is invisible today, but a March/April row that appears out of order would print out of order. Similarly `formatCents(cents)` hardcodes no currency, so a mixed-currency CSV would be summed into one bogus total and labelled `USD` (latent; current example is all-USD).

**3. `src/cli.js:9` — unguarded `readFileSync` and no exit/failure handling** (minor, no test coverage)
There is no `test/cli.test.js`, so no failing test points here. A missing or unreadable file throws a raw `ENOENT` stack trace instead of the usage-style message used at line 6, and `console.log(report(...))` swallows the empty-report case as a bare newline. Also note `report` output has no trailing newline (report.js:15), so the CLI relies on `console.log` to terminate the line.

## Cross-file bugs that also decide the report tests

**4. `src/csv.js:3-7` — no quote handling and no `\r` handling** (critical)
Splits on `,` and `\n` only, so quoted commas split cells, doubled `""` are not unescaped, and CRLF leaves `\r` in the last header/cell value.
Explains: `csv.test.js` "quoted commas stay in one cell", "doubled quotes are a literal quote", "windows line endings"; also corrupts the `examples/march.csv` rows (`"Coffee, beans"`, `"Books, ""used"""`, trailing `\r`) and therefore blocks "march report".

**5. `src/money.js:3` — `toCents` truncates instead of rounding** (major)
`Math.floor(Number(amount) * 100)` turns `"0.29"` into 28.
Explains: `money.test.js` "toCents rounds instead of truncating". Would silently shave a cent off any exact-half/thirds amount in the report (e.g. amounts like `1.10` are fine, but the contract is wrong).

**6. `src/money.js:9` — cents are not zero-padded** (major)
`` `${abs % 100}` `` prints `USD 15.2` for 1520 cents.
Explains: `money.test.js` "formatCents pads cents", and is the second reason `report.test.js:14` "march report" can't pass even with a correct `totalsByMonth` (expected `USD 15.20`).
